statusText: CME equity futures are halted for thirteen of the twenty-four published hours, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window, leaving the 22:00Z Sunday restart as the only slot carrying materially elevated conditional risk. The one new verified item this run widens the confirmed Saudi interception perimeter to five named sites while leaving the outcome record - intercepted, no casualties, no damage - intact.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 18, still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: A wider confirmed attack perimeter but an unchanged outcome record: Saudi Arabia reports interceptions at five named sites with no casualties or damage, every primary mark re-verifies unchanged, and the escalation-versus-supply-repair balance carries intact into the 22:00Z restart
body:
Thirteen of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final eleven contain the 22:00Z restart, the hours after it and the Asian session that follows. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run and every one is unchanged: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44 inside a 14.80-15.63 day range and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range. Crude settled easier for a third consecutive session, WTI at 100.30 and Brent at 103.87, although WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month because the East-West pipeline has been offline since the 11 September strike.

One item genuinely advanced since the previous assessment, and it cuts both ways. The confirmed attack perimeter is wider than previously published: Saudi authorities now confirm that the ballistic missile attempt on Riyadh was accompanied by attacks on Yanbu, Taif, Baysh and Farasan, and state that all of them were intercepted or thwarted. The outcome record attached to those five sites is unchanged and remains benign - no casualties and no damage reported, with Aramco declining to comment on the Houthi claim of massive fires - although separately, debris from an intercepted drone killed a Yemeni resident of Saudi Arabia on Thursday. So the intent and reach of the campaign is now verified as broader, while its realised effect is still not verified as material. That is an increase in the breadth of the escalation evidence without a corresponding increase in the evidence of transmission, and under the risk definition used here it belongs in Stress and in the width of the conditional distribution, not in Tail.

The rest of the ledger stands as before and was re-verified. On the escalatory side, the State Department issued alerts on Saturday evening covering Israel, Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE and Oman, warning that the conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly, urging Americans not already in the region to seriously reconsider travel to and through it, and flagging possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruption. On the de-escalatory side, US Central Command reports Hormuz crude and LNG throughput over the past fortnight at a six-month high, with more than a billion barrels shipped through the strait in the last couple of months and Iran exporting zero barrels under enforcement; reporting on Friday's easier crude tape attributed the weekly loss to fading Saudi export fears. A weekend that is escalatory in intent and repairing in supply at the same time remains the classic setup for two-way price discovery at the reopen rather than a persistent one-way path.

The macro backdrop is restrictive and unchanged. The FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023, and the accompanying projections were hawkish: sixteen of eighteen participants expect at least one further increase this year and four see two, with the median 2026 dot at 4.1%. The H.15 release dated 18 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.29% as of 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%, and the 10-year has climbed back toward 5% since the decision. That backdrop is the persistent named driver carried across the published hours, and a yield extension during Asian trade is the cross-asset condition most likely to slow the Tail decay published after the restart.

Two index-level checkpoints sit just outside the window. The Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance is confirmed and takes effect at Monday's cash open, lifting SpaceX from a weight of about 1.28% to 2.82% on Friday's closing prices; more than 200 products tracking the benchmark, with over $800bn in assets including the $482bn Invesco QQQ Trust, must adjust. Separately, a US-China meeting has been reported for the coming week, but it is not confirmed by Beijing; because the timing is materially uncertain it is omitted from the published calendar rather than guessed, and is carried only as an unconfirmed checkpoint. Neither item is a path variable for the hours published here, and mechanical rebalancing turnover is not the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures.

Friday's tape supports carrying no structural amplifier forward. The session was rotational rather than uniform - the Nasdaq added 0.7% while the Dow closed about 95 points lower and the S&P 500 rose 0.2%. Latest-session internals corroborate that split: four of the eight Nasdaq megacaps closed higher and four lower, with a mean change near +0.24%, while semiconductors led at roughly +1.28% mean, with QCOM an outlier at -5.82%, and both software industry groups closed lower. That shared context is delayed latest-session data and is used here only as confirmation, never as live NQ price evidence; this run it was also collected outside its freshness window and its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so it carries less weight than in earlier runs.

Current Tail stays at the closed-venue floor of 5: no venue is open and no structure has been observed. Stress is published at 30, unchanged, because the wider confirmed perimeter and the unchanged benign outcome record offset one another. Confidence is published at 74, also unchanged: the newly verified interception detail, the corroborated Hormuz throughput figures and a full re-verification of the seven-day calendar offset one more hour of distance from the Friday tape and a shared-context file that is now stale and partial. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the published 24 hours. Tokyo cash equities open at 00:00Z and provide the first regional cash reference since Friday; the China loan prime rate decision has already resolved, held at 3.00% and 3.50% for a sixteenth month, matching all 21 forecasts in the Reuters survey. The first Monday catalyst, the Goolsbee remarks at 10:30Z, sits beyond the end of the window, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail is published at 5 through the early halt, drifting up in single steps that track time-to-restart rather than observed structure, reaching a window high of 18 at the restart before easing through the Asian session. Every published hour stays inside the low Tail band and the EA_ON mapping, and no danger window is identified.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first thirteen slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 across the final four slots. Stress opened at 21, drifted through 22, 23 and 24 across the Saturday afternoon and evening, stepped to 26 shortly after midnight, eased to 25 and then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation headlines landed, settling at 28 and then 30 across the final two slots. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence started at 77, decayed to a 72 trough at 21:00Z as distance from the Friday tape grew, then recovered into the mid-70s as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Thirteen of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final eleven contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian and European hours after it. Cash closed Friday 18 September and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, beyond its end, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for the current hour, then steps to 6 and 7, pauses, and rises to 9 by mid-afternoon before advancing one point per hour to a pre-restart 15 at 21:00Z. It reaches the window high of 18 at the 22:00Z restart, eases to 17 for the first full hour and then decays through 15, 14, 13, 12 and 11 before flattening at 10 for the final four hours. That drift tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure and stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping in every published hour. Mode is published as event/whipsaw for the restart and the hour after it, then mixed for the first three Asian hours, reflecting expected two-way discovery against a weekend that produced escalation of intent and supply repair at the same time; it returns to normal for the final six hours on the base case that repricing has cleared. The Nasdaq-100 rebalance effective at Monday's cash open sits beyond the window and is carried as a checkpoint, not an amplifier.
